title: newState races concurrent Peer/deliver in Chat/set and Contact/set
description: Chat/set and Contact/set (and Message/set) all capture old_state inside one lock scope and then re-acquire a second lock to read new_state. Between the two lock acquires, a concurrent Peer/deliver can increment the state counter. The returned newState then includes that concurrent write, causing the client to skip that concurrent change in its next /changes window — it will never see those changes because newState is now past them. RFC 8620 §5.3 requires newState to describe the state after THIS call's writes. Fix: fetch new_state inside the same lock scope as the writes (either extend the existing scope or use a single SQLite transaction that returns the counter after the insert).
